kenji: heads-up — noticed a BLEU drop in the multilingual bring-up for rwdx/multilang-3b-int8 when inputs include mixed directionality (CJK prefix + Arabic suffix).

kenji: quick numbers from today's nightly: fp16 baseline BLEU=34.2, int8 drop to 28.7 on our news-ml20 testset (subset w/ zh+ar concat).

maya: ouch. is it consistent across lengths?

kenji: seems length-dependent. short prompts (<=64 tokens) the gap is ~2 BLEU points. long-prefix cases (>=512 tokens, especially when prefix is mostly CJK) show the biggest regression (4–7 BLEU).

vikram: can you paste a repro example? might be tokenization detok mismatch or KV-cache alignment after quantized kernels.

kenji: repro below (sanitized):

```
# repro command (eval harness)
python eval.py --model rwdx/multilang-3b --quant int8 --dataset news-ml20 --filter "lang:zh+ar" --max-src 1024 --batch 1
```

kenji: sample src (truncated):

"这是一个关于经济的报道。
...长段落...

هذا ملحق باللغة العربية يتبع النص الصيني"

sophie: interesting — do you see different token counts between fp16 and int8 runs? maybe tokenizer table shuffled during quant build?

kenji: token counts identical for the raw tokenizer. but detokenized outputs differ: punctuation/clitics in Arabic come out shifted or duplicated. looks like a subtoken boundary shift near the CJK->Arabic boundary.

maya: possible causes: 1) quantization-induced kernel rounding affecting KV-cache offsets, 2) tokenizer normalization bug in streaming detok changes, 3) postprocessing/opposite-direction joins.

eval-bot: ran quick diff on 50 samples: 38/50 show alignment drift at the script boundary, 22/50 produced extra whitespace or merged punctuation in Arabic suffix. mean BLEU drop 5.3 for those 38. logs uploaded: https://artifacts.internal/runs/1938456123/diff

vikram: thanks. can you bisect to the exact commit that introduced the int8 runtime change? last int8 rollup merged in commit 7f3a1c9 (kernel reorder + cache packing).

kenji: starting a bisect now. tagging infra-bot to spin a dedicated runner with both fp16/int8 for longer contexts. @infra-bot ?

infra-bot: scheduled: ci-infer-serial-17 (worker: gpu-a100-80gb) — will run bisect jobs in parallel across commits. ETA ~45m.

sophie: while bisect runs, can we try a quick hack: disable cache packing in int8 path to see if it alleviates boundary shift? I can build a dev wheel and drop it into the runner.

maya: also try forcing tokenizer to emit explicit ZWNJ/ZWJ markers at script transitions to see if detok step was fragile. add a preprocess wrapper that inserts U+200C at boundary for 10 samples.

kenji: good ideas. I'll queue two jobs: (A) int8 without cache packing, (B) int8 + ZWNJ insert.

kenji: job A started -> preliminary: BLEU improves from 28.7 -> 32.1 on the same subset. still behind fp16 34.2 but much better.

maya: that strongly implicates cache packing behavior in int8. can you capture KV-cache dumps at boundary step to inspect offsets?

kenji: capturing dumps now. sample diff: in packed int8 run the start index for the Arabic suffix tokens is off by +2 in some layers causing alignment errors during attention slicing.

vikram: that explains duplication/shift. indexing bug triggered by quant packing math (int division rounding). looks like floor vs ceil mismatch when computing block counts for packed rows.

sophie: if it's rounding, the fix should be straightforward: unify to consistent ceil() across compile-time and runtime. but need regression tests.

eval-bot: suggested tests added to eval harness: 1) mixed-script long-prefix regression case, 2) compare token-aligned perplexity slice at boundaries.

kenji: created PR #4179 with a patch to use ceil in packing (and a defensive assert on expected kv sizes). linking logs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rwdx/pull/4179

maya: can someone run PR on dedicated runner? if PR fixes, we should promote to int8 canary and re-run full news-ml20.

infra-bot: PR runner queued on ci-infer-serial-17.

vikram: also let's check quantization calibration tables. if kernel reorder interacts weirdly with packing, we may need to add a calibration test to CI that includes mixed-directionality texts.

kenji: agreed. adding a calibration check is in the PR description.

sophie: follow-up: we should add a short doc in eng-ml about this class of failure — "script-boundary KV packing edgecases" — to help triage future model bring-ups (esp. multilingual). I'll draft one after the PR lands.

maya: timeline? if PR fixes in canary, we should re-run nightly int8 full eval and update the model catalog notes (flagging prior int8 runs as impacted).

kenji: if infra tests pass, I'll cut a canary snapshot and run full eval tonight. will post results here.

infra-bot: PR runner completed: all tests green on canary.

kenji: canary int8 re-eval (same subset) BLEU=34.0 — within noise of fp16 34.2. pushing canary to nightly full-run now.

maya: excellent. thanks everyone. next steps: 1) merge PR 4179, 2) add CI regression tests, 3) doc draft, 4) update model catalog notes + rollback guidance.

sophie: +1 on doc. I'll pair with kenji for the write-up.

kenji: thanks — will post final summary & links once merged. :thumbsup:

eval-bot: final artifacts: https://artifacts.internal/runs/1938456123/canary-report and diff tarball.

vikram: great resolution. tagging this thread for postmortems if full-nightly shows no surprises.

kenji: closing loop here for now — will update last_message_ts when full-nightly completes.
